findings.problem: The succ case does the same one-layer reduction twice, once for p with x none and once for p₁ with x₁ none. Each time it applies sumOptionSpecialization_stableOrZero. It then splits on zero or stable. It also derives multiaffinity of the specialization. Finally it rewrites with partialSpecialization_option and, in the zero case, partialSpecialization_zero. The second copy is the first one with p, x, hmulti, hstable replaced by p₁, x₁, hm₁, hfirst. The two layers are also unfolded by hand with `change`, `let`, and the nested `rcases`. Any change to the peeling step has to be made in both copies.
findings.proposed_change: Add a one-layer lemma. For `{κ τ : Type*} [Finite τ]`, assume `ih : ∀ (q : MvPolynomial (κ ⊕ τ) ℂ) (y : κ → ℝ), IsComplexMultiaffine q → IsUpperHalfPlaneStable q → partialSpecialization q y = 0 ∨ IsUpperHalfPlaneStable (partialSpecialization q y)`. Conclude the same statement for `Option κ` (that is, for `p : MvPolynomial (Option κ ⊕ τ) ℂ` and `x : Option κ → ℝ`). Proof sketch: `rcases sumOptionSpecialization_stableOrZero p (x none) hmulti hstable with h0 | h1`. In the zero case, `left; rw [partialSpecialization_option p x hmulti, h0, partialSpecialization_zero]`. In the stable case, `rw [partialSpecialization_option p x hmulti]; exact ih _ _ (sumOptionSpecialization_multiaffine p (x none) hmulti) h1`. The succ case then reduces to `optionPartialSpecialization_stableOrZero (optionPartialSpecialization_stableOrZero (fun q y hq hs ↦ ih q y hq hs))`, where ih is specialized to the same τ. The type `PairVariables (n+1)` unfolds definitionally to `Option (Option (PairVariables n))`, so `exact` should work after at most one `change`. The `Finite τ` argument is passed along as an instance. The Option layers keep τ unchanged, so no universe problem arises.
findings.benefit: The roughly 30-line nested case split becomes a lemma of about 10 lines plus a two-fold application. The peeling logic then exists in one place. The induction step reads as "two layers of Option", which matches PairVariables. The same helper also covers any other induction over Option-nested index types.
